concepts.title: Turning Tides: New Powers of the Age
concepts.definition: In the eleventh and twelfth centuries the tide of power turned: newer dynasties pressed old ones, trade caravans and fleets grew, and forces from beyond the north-west began to enter India.
concepts.key_idea: Centuries of settled kingdoms met new claimants, and India entered another age of readjustment.

concepts.title: The Cholas at Their Height
concepts.definition: The Cholas of Thanjavur stood at their height: Rajaraja and Rajendra built a navy, sent expeditions across the seas, raised the Brihadishvara temple, and ran a rich administration of villages and temples.
concepts.key_idea: The Cholas showed what a sea-facing power could be: temple, fleet and village assembly working together.

concepts.title: Invasions from the North-West
concepts.definition: From beyond the mountains came raiders: Mahmud of Ghazni repeatedly plundered the temples and towns of north-west India, and near the century's end Muhammad of Ghor's armies stayed to found a new sultanate.
concepts.key_idea: Wealth without united defence invited raids: India withstood the shocks, but the age changed its rulers and its maps.

concepts.title: Caravans, Coasts and Trade
concepts.definition: Caravans of traders crossed the passes and dusty roads, while ports on both coasts tied India to Southeast Asia and the Arab lands, moving textiles, spices, horses and ideas in every direction.
concepts.key_idea: Trade kept India rich and connected even in turbulent times: goods moved when armies could not.

solution_template.explain: Rich, famed temples and cities lay close to the north-western passes.
